name: On-Prem Jira → Jira Cloud Migration (Project Skyline)

raid.title: Critical path concentrated on one engineer
raid.description: Sven Lindqvist owns four of the eleven critical-path tasks (tooling, pilot, bulk, reconciliation). Illness, churn, or competing priorities on that one person stalls the whole migration.
raid.mitigation: Cross-train a second migration engineer on the tooling and wave runbook; pair on the pilot and bulk waves so the chain isn't single-threaded.

provenance.reasoning: Key-person risk surfaced by the schedule: a single owner sits on most of the zero-float chain, so their availability gates the launch.

evidence.statement: The critical path runs through a single owner: Sven Lindqvist owns 4 of 11 critical-path tasks.

raid.title: Critical plugins have no Cloud equivalent
raid.description: At least three critical marketplace plugins can't be re-pointed to Cloud; each needs a replacement, a scripted rebuild, or a decision to live without it before users migrate.
raid.mitigation: Audit every plugin for Cloud compatibility early; gate user migration on the plugin sign-off; budget rebuild time for the three known gaps.

provenance.reasoning: The PRD calls plugins the scary part and names three with no direct Cloud path — a high-likelihood, high-impact risk to the wave plan.

evidence.source_quote: at least three of our critical plugins have no direct Cloud equivalent

raid.title: Contractor budget not yet approved
raid.description: The bulk migration depends on two contractors, but Finance approval for contractor spend is not secured yet, blocking onboarding.

provenance.reasoning: An open, live blocker (not a hypothetical): onboarding cannot start until the spend is approved, and it gates the bulk waves.

evidence.source_quote:
contractor spend has to be approved by Finance before anyone gets
onboarded

raid.title: Formal per-owner data reconciliation assumed
raid.description: The plan assumes a formal reconciliation step signed off by each project owner (not a spot check). If a spot check is deemed enough, the reconciliation task shrinks.

provenance.reasoning: The PRD leaves this open but says to assume formal for now — a planning assumption worth surfacing so it can be confirmed.

raid.title: Lift-and-shift; defer workflow redesign
raid.description: Workflows are migrated as-is; redesigning them is explicitly out of scope and deferred to a later project.
raid.rationale: Scope discipline against the hard license-expiry wall: workflow cleanup is a separate later project so it can't jeopardise the migration deadline.

provenance.reasoning: A recorded scope decision from the PRD, captured so the rationale survives into the plan of record.

evidence.source_quote:
We lift-and-shift; workflow cleanup
is a later project
